admin.attachments.heading: Attachments
admin.slug_note: The address is made from the English title, and does not change after the first confirmation.

admin.more_note: Returning undoes an undeployed confirmation, back to what the site shows now. Taking down removes this post in the next deployment; the confirmed text in both languages and the genealogy records are kept.
admin.settings.lede_html: Things you set once and rarely change. What you check each time you publish is on the Site screen.
admin.identity.heading: Blog settings
admin.identity.note_html: The name, byline, introduction and the terms your writing carries. They apply to every page: once saved, they appear under what the next deployment changes on the Site screen, and reach readers when you deploy.
admin.identity.name: Blog name
admin.identity.author: Author name
admin.license.note_html: How readers may use the writing on this blog. It is separate from this tool's code licence (MIT); unless you choose otherwise, all rights are reserved.
admin.destination.heading: Deployment destination
admin.destination.local: Writing files to a local folder
admin.destination.homepage: Opening a pull request on a GitHub Pages repository
admin.destination.local_note_html: The finished static files are written to that folder. Neither a GitHub account nor gh is needed; put the folder wherever you like (any static host, rsync, a plain copy). To serve the site at example.com/blog/, set the base path to /blog/. Files this tool did not write are never deleted or overwritten.
admin.destination.homepage_note_html: Pages serves / (root) of this branch. The blog always lives at /blog/. You need to be signed in to the GitHub CLI (gh).
admin.import.lede_html: Bring in Markdown writing you already have, with its pictures, a whole folder at a time. The folder is only read, never changed. Pictures stay where the writing points to them, so no link in the text is rewritten.
admin.import.folder_note_html: The absolute path of the folder your writing is in. Every subfolder is scanned. Pictures are found whether they sit beside the writing or in a subfolder such as images/.
admin.progress.heading: Deployment in progress
admin.progress.pr: Open the pull request on GitHub ↗
admin.progress.recovery_note: Use this only if preparing or sending was interrupted and the deployment is stuck in progress. It does not cancel a remote pull request; it records a failure so the same release can be tried again.

admin.changes.title: What this deployment changes

admin.history.note: Every release and every attempt is kept. Taking something down does not delete past Git history or copies cached elsewhere.

flow.deploy.lede_none: First choose, on the Settings screen, where confirmed posts are deployed.
flow.deploy.lede_folder: Confirmed posts are written to the folder you chose. Once the files are read back and verified, it is done; there is nothing to wait for.
flow.deploy.lede_pr: Confirmed posts go to your Pages repository as one pull request. When you merge it on GitHub, Pages updates the site.
flow.deploy.deployed_folder: Written to the folder. Every file was read back and verified.
flow.deploy.deployed_pr: Pull request opened. Merge it on GitHub, then choose Check deployment.
flow.deploy.note_folder: This deployment stopped while writing to the folder. Check deployment reads the files back to see whether they match.
flow.deploy.note_pr: Merge the pull request on GitHub, then choose Check deployment. Until it is merged and Pages has built, it stays in progress; you cannot start another deployment meanwhile, but you can keep preparing posts.
flow.deploy.rollback_folder: Roll back and write to the folder
flow.deploy.hint.running: Check the deployment in progress first.
flow.deploy.hint.no_destination: First choose a folder or a Pages repository under Deployment destination on the Settings screen.

flow.deploy.hint.retry_failed: Nothing has changed since the failed release, so that release is sent again as it is.
flow.deploy.hint.prepared_folder: Writes the prepared release to the folder as it is.
flow.deploy.hint.prepared_pr: Opens a pull request with the prepared release.
flow.deploy.hint.same_as_site: This is the same as the site now.
flow.deploy.hint.nothing: The site and your confirmed posts agree. Changes appear here once you confirm a post.
flow.deploy.hint.rollback_folder: Builds a new release with this content and writes it to the folder.
flow.deploy.hint.rollback_pr: Builds a new release with this content and opens a pull request.
flow.deploy.hint.missing_folder: The site is unchanged, but this folder does not have it yet. A release with the same content is built and written.
flow.deploy.hint.missing_pr: The site is unchanged, but this repository does not have it yet. A release with the same content is built and a pull request opened.
flow.deploy.hint.folder: Builds a release from your confirmed posts and writes it to the folder. The files are finished at once; there is no merge to wait for.
flow.deploy.hint.pr: Builds a release from your confirmed posts and opens a pull request. You merge it yourself on GitHub.
flow.checked.running_folder: Still checking. Try again in a moment.
flow.checked.running_pr: Not merged yet, or Pages is still building. Try again in a moment.
flow.checked.succeeded_folder: The files in the folder match the release.
flow.checked.failed: The deployment was recorded as failed. You can try the same release again.
flow.import.state.imported: Imported. You will find it in the editor's library.
flow.import.state.attached: The missing pictures are attached. The writing itself is unchanged.
flow.import.state.nothing: There was nothing to import, so nothing was saved.

flow.import.hint.again: To import another folder, scan again above.
